instruction: We represent Drulun Therapeutics, Inc., which buys finished drug product from Pruvax Biologics Manufacturing, LLC under a supply agreement. Drulun wants a clear picture of where it stands under the current contract documents so it can decide what to raise with Pruvax. Please review everything in the matter folder: the supply agreement (drulun_pruvax_supply_agreement.md), Order Form No. 3 (order_form_no_3.md), the data processing addendum (data_processing_addendum.md), and the November 2023 prior draft of the supply agreement (supply_agreement_draft_nov2023.md). Then send me a memo that lists each issue you find. For each one, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters to Drulun, and recommend a fix. Rank the issues by how much they matter to the client, and flag anything that needs a quick decision or action from Drulun. Keep it practical: I want to be able to use it to brief the client without rewriting it.

rubric.text: The response identifies that the Data Processing Addendum selects Delaware law and Delaware courts, which control for data-related claims, so those claims are split from the New York-governed supply claims.
hints: laws of the State of Delaware

rubric.text: The response locates the Delaware governing law and forum issue in Section 12 of the Data Processing Addendum.
The response explains why the Delaware governing law and forum split matters to Drulun.
The response recommends a fix for the Delaware governing law and forum split.
hints: conform the DPA to New York law

rubric.text: The response identifies that Order Form No. 3 defines 'Delivery' as tender to the first carrier at Pruvax's facility, and that this definition overrides the Supply Agreement's definition of Delivery as receipt in Edison, New Jersey.
The response locates the redefinition of 'Delivery' in Section 4 of Order Form No. 3.
The response explains why the Order Form's redefinition of 'Delivery' matters to Drulun.
The response recommends a fix for the Order Form's redefinition of 'Delivery'.
The response identifies that Drulun's non-renewal notice dated August 14, 2026 missed the 180-day deadline of August 4, 2026, so the Supply Agreement likely auto-renewed.
The response locates the recorded non-renewal notice in Recital C of Order Form No. 3.
The response explains why the late non-renewal notice matters to Drulun.
The response recommends a fix for the late non-renewal notice.
The response states that the Supply Agreement's order-of-precedence clause (Section 17.3) lets other contract documents override the Supply Agreement in specified subject areas.
The response states that the Supply Agreement's Effective Date is February 1, 2024.
The response is a memo that ranks or orders the issues by their importance to Drulun.
The response flags at least one item as needing a quick decision or prompt action from Drulun.
The response claims that Drulun's non-renewal notice dated August 14, 2026 was timely.
The response claims that the Supply Agreement's definition of Delivery (receipt in Edison, New Jersey) governs the batches covered by Order Form No. 3.
